choices: The cost of each additional unit of output
The wage paid to each worker
All input combinations with the same total cost
All input combinations with the same output
explain: Iso-cost = same cost: C = wL + rK. Same output is an isoquant. Cost of an extra unit is marginal cost.

stem: With K on the vertical axis, the vertical intercept of the isocost line is:
explain: Setting L = 0 in K = C/r - (w/r)L gives K = C/r, the most capital the budget buys. C/w is the horizontal intercept and -w/r is the slope.

stem: True or false: If the budget C rises and input prices stay the same, the isocost line shifts out parallel to the old line.
explain: True. The slope -w/r does not depend on C; both intercepts grow by the same percentage.

stem: Holding C and r fixed, the wage rises. The isocost line:
choices: Becomes steeper; the horizontal intercept moves in
Becomes flatter; the horizontal intercept moves out
Becomes steeper; the vertical intercept moves up
explain: Slope -w/r grows in magnitude and C/w shrinks. C/r is unchanged, so the vertical intercept stays put.

stem: True or false: The isocost equation C = wL + rK is printed on the equation sheet.
explain: False. Only the slope -w/r is on the sheet. Know C = wL + rK and the intercepts.

stem: Budget $1,000, wage $10, rental rate $25. What is the most labor the firm can hire if it uses no capital?
Budget $1,000, wage $10, rental rate $25. What is the slope of the isocost line (K on the vertical axis)?
Budget $1,500, wage $30, rental rate $50. What is the most capital the firm can rent if it hires no labor?
A firm spends on 20 workers at $15 each and 10 machines at $40 each. What is its total cost on this isocost?
Budget $1,000, rental rate $25. The wage doubles from $10 to $20. What is the new maximum amount of labor?
explain: C/w = 1,000/20 = 50, down from 100 (slides p. 34). The vertical intercept stays at 40.

stem: A CEO cuts the weekly production budget by 50%. Prices are unchanged. What happens to the isocost line?
choices: It rotates around the vertical intercept
It shifts in parallel; both intercepts halve
explain: Only C changed, so the slope -w/r is the same and both intercepts, C/w and C/r, are cut in half (slides p. 33).

stem: Union negotiations lower the wage while machine rental rates stay the same. On a graph with K vertical, the firm's isocost:
choices: Pivots out along the labor axis and gets flatter
Pivots up along the capital axis and gets steeper
explain: Lower w raises C/w (horizontal intercept moves out) and reduces w/r (flatter). C/r is unchanged.

stem: AI software rental prices fall while wages stay the same. Which intercept of the isocost line (K = AI hours on the vertical axis) changes?
explain: C/r rises when r falls, so the vertical intercept moves up. C/w is unchanged.
